Software Engineer to Software Approver This is something that of 2024. Addy Osmani referred to as “The 70% problem” at the end This 30% of friction meant that AI was good for things like prototyping, MVPs and learning aids rather than critical production code. Fast-forward to today and the current leading models have made this much less of a problem, but it’s not gone entirely! The quality of the code produced has vastly improved but the cognitive burden of understanding it still rests on us mere Software Approvers. 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

Skill Decline 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

Skill Decline Not REALLY but it shares a lot of similar behaviours. • Your brain is a muscle - if you don’t work it out it weakens • Reading code is not the same as writing code We just don’t seem to retain information as well when we read it compared to when we produce it (this is something known as the Generation Effect) • We’re offloading our thinking to these AI models but we don’t seem to be putting that freed up mental capacity towards more critical thinking. Instead the current (admittedly limited) research suggests it’s causing us to get lazier. 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

Higher confidence in GenAI’s ability to perform a task is related to less critical thinking effort. https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3706598.3713778 The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported Reductions in Cognitive Effort and Con dence Effects From a Survey of Knowledge Workers fi 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

Skill Decline • It’s not just our programming skills that are at risk! • As Adriana Villela highlights in their post From Builder to Architect we’re losing our: • • Troubleshooting skills • Writing skills • Motivation to learn It’s also having an impact on our collaboration skills! • Ideas and features are now planned out with AI • Colleagues aren’t discussing work up front so aren’t building up a shared context 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

The conversation that feels slower than prompting alone is doing something the prompt cannot do. Left of the Loop by Simon Schrottner 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

The Human Cost 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

The Human Cost • • • • Replacing existing staff with AI is just silly (and frankly a horrible thing to do) • Klarna replaced 700 employees with AI - a year later they reversed that decision • A leaked Duolingo memo about going AI-first sparked online controversy and caused the company to walk back the decision Some companies seem to be using AI as an excuse to reduce employee numbers to appease investors Hiring freezes are on the rise as more companies asses if their existing staff can Burnout incoming! do more work with AI Callback to Engineer → Approver “59% [of hiring managers] admit they emphasise AI [for] hiring freezes or layoffs […]” - ResumeTemplates.com 2026 survey of 1,000 US hiring managers 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

The Human Cost • Stanford Digital Economy Lab found that employment, in the US, of young workers in AI-heavy industries fell ~19% (fell ~13% the previous year) • The SignalFire State of Tech Talent Report 2026 found hiring of new grads in tech dropped to only 8% at “Big Tech” and 3% at startups - going down year on year! • For the new grads that are being hired there’s an increased bias towards “Elite” universities (e.g. MIT, Harvard) - up 10% since 2022 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social

The Human Cost Couple this with the skill decline, lack of motivation to learn and reduced communication within teams and you have a shortage of senior engineers within a generation. 😱 🐘 @Marcus@k8s.social | 🌐 MarcusNoble.com | 🦋 @averagemarcus.bsky.social
